segments.text: Good morning. I am Dr. Iverson. We have not met before. Could you tell me your name?
Camila Fabricius. Thank you for seeing me.
You are very welcome, Camila. Let us take this in order. Tell me what has brought you here today.
Well, it is my family, really. My grandfather on my father's side died of a heart attack, and he was only 52.
Thank you for telling me. So, there is cardiovascular disease in your family?
Yes. And ever since I worked that out, I have not been able to stop thinking about it. Is that the sort of thing that gets passed down?
A family history of heart and circulatory disease is one of the things we take into account. That is exactly why it is worth looking at properly.
Right. I was rather afraid you would say that.
Right.
Let me explain what I am talking about.
Let me explain what I mean before you worry. Taking it into account is not the same as saying you have anything.
Okay. Okay, that does help a little.
Good. Now, tell me about your own health.
I am healthy, as far as I know. No illnesses at all. I eat well and I look after myself.
And exercise?
I train regularly. That part I am actually consistent about, which I suppose is something.
It is. And it matters. Let us go through the rest step-by-step, so you know what I am doing and why.
Please do. I would much rather know what is happening than sit here guessing.
First, I look at you. You look healthy, Camilla. There is nothing about your general appearance that concerns me.
Is that really something you can tell just by looking at someone?
It is part of the picture, not the whole of it. That is why I measure and test as well.
All right. So what comes next?
Your blood pressure. I have measured it at 138 over 83.
Is that bad? It sounds high when you say it out loud like that.
I am recording it as today's measurement, and it will be looked at together with the tests I want to arrange.
So you are not telling me it is fine, exactly?
I am telling you what I measured, and that I do not draw conclusions from one reading on it.
That is fair. I would rather have that than be brushed off with a pat on the shoulder.
I will not brush you off. What we are doing today is a preventive health check because of the family disposition you described.
Preventive? So this is a check rather than a hunt for something already wrong with me?
Precisely. You have understood it exactly. Does that distinction make sense?
It does. Sorry.
I am a little scattered. I spent 20 minutes in a queue at the post office and arrived flustered.
That queue defeats everyone. You are here in good time.
Thank you. Back to the tests, then. What exactly are you going to do?
Two things. I will take blood samples, and I will record an electrocardiogram, which is a tracing of the heart's electrical activity.
An electrocardiogram. Is that uncomfortable?
Uncomfortable? I have never had one.
Small stickers on the skin and a short recording. That is all there is to it.
Are you following me so far?
I am. Blood samples and a tracing of my heart.
That is the plan. We will go through what they show once we have them.
Thank you. I feel better having a plan than sitting at home wondering about it.
